topic: What trade-offs exist between array size and radiation efficiency for SIW arrays in high-gain inter-satellite antennas?
consensus_response: Increasing the array size of SIW (Substrate Integrated Waveguide) arrays enhances gain but introduces higher insertion loss due to longer substrate length, impacting radiation efficiency. Larger arrays also increase mutual coupling and interference between elements, reducing performance. Periodic Boundary Conditions (PBCs) can mitigate these issues by simulating infinite periodic structures, decoupling elements, and improving overall efficiency. However, PBCs may introduce artificial coupling between unit cells. Inaccurate material properties during design stages cause discrepancies between simulated and measured gains. Optimized hybrid feeding topologies and precise fabrication techniques are essential to balance good performance with compact configuration while considering fabrication tolerances.
reference_context: The reference context provides various technical aspects of SIW arrays, including the impact of array size on radiation efficiency, mutual coupling, and interference. It also discusses the use of PBCs, hybrid feeding topologies, and material properties on the design and performance of SIW arrays.
